title: TREX-F: TRustability of Electronics using X-ray based Fingerprinting
problem: Counterfeit and tampered printed circuit boards (PCBs) infiltrate the electronics supply chain, posing risks to business and security.
motivation: Authenticating PCBs is essential for maintaining supply chain integrity and preventing circulation of forged electronics.
method: TREX-F leverages inherent physical defects (solder irregularities, material deposition, microscopic anomalies) captured by X-ray microscopy at specific angles. Uses computer vision techniques (Canny edge detection, contour detection, PCA, SIFT) to extract unique fingerprints from X-ray CT slices, converting them into QR and data-matrix codes for authentication.
key_novelty: X-ray-based physical fingerprinting for PCB authentication using computer vision analysis.
contributions: X-ray imaging-based PCB fingerprint extraction using anomaly detection
Computer vision-based feature extraction (Canny, contour, PCA, SIFT)
QR and data-matrix code generation for quick authentication
~95% average authentication accuracy with ~0.1% false acceptance rate
limitations: Limited to three specific PCB types; generalization to other designs unclear.
